sources.title: Default Liquidity Tiers on dYdX Chain

claims.text: Hyperliquid uses a rolling 14-day weighted volume system for fee tiers, with separate perp and spot schedules and additional staking-tier discounts.

dYdX describes a maker-taker model in which taker fees are based on trailing 30-day USD volume across perpetual order books, and the current schedule is surfaced through the dYdX interface or linked docs.
Hyperliquid funding is paid hourly, uses a premium component against the spot oracle price, has a fixed interest component described in the docs, and is capped at 4% per hour.
dYdX funding in the default v4 software is calculated from premium samples and is subject to governance-controlled parameters.
Hyperliquid liquidations occur when equity falls below maintenance margin, first route liquidation attempts through market orders on the book, and may use the liquidator vault as a backstop.

dYdX Chain liquidations use protocol-generated matches and an insurance-fund mechanism under default v4 software assumptions; official documentation warns that up to the entire remaining account value may be taken as a liquidation penalty.
Hyperliquid oracle prices are published by validators every three seconds and are used for funding, mark price, margining, liquidations, and TP/SL triggers.
dYdX oracle prices are validator-determined aggregated prices used for collateralization, liquidation checks, and triggerable order types.
dYdX liquidity tiers group markets into standardized risk parameters and can affect initial margin fraction, maintenance margin fraction, impact notional, and safety-tier handling.
The comparison does not verify overall liquidity, volume leadership, security superiority, or user eligibility by jurisdiction; those remain outside this source set.
